newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace challenges Monsanto soybean patent.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace challenges Monsanto soybean patent.

text.p: The environmental organisation Greenpeace said on Thursday it had filed a legal challenge against a patent granted to U.S. chemicals giant Monsanto for genetically altered soybeans.
In a complaint to the European Patent Office, Greenpeace contended living things could not be patented under European law, Greenpeace activist Benedikt Haerlin told journalists.
Environmentalists in Germany have been calling for labelling of soybeans to enable consumers to avoid the genetically altered products if they so choose.
The Monsanto soybeans were first imported to Germany last November.
Monsanto obtained the patent in July 1996 covering 18 plants genetically altered to be resistant to its weed-killer Roundup.

Haerlin said the Greenpeace complaint had a good chance of succeeding. In a statement issued in Brussels, the organisation said it had already successfully challenged the patenting of a genetically altered plant in 1995.
Greenpeace claims that patenting of genetically altered plants and animals endangers biodiversity and the independence of the agricultural sector.

Farmers in the U.S. who grow Roundup-resistant soybeans are forced to buy only that herbicide, and must give Monsanto access to their fields, Greenpeace says. They are also unable to obtain seeds from their own harvests.
Greenpeace also intends to file a complaint against any attempt to patent the sheep Dolly cloned at Scotland's Roslin Institute, Haerlin said.
